trajectory_messages.content:
I'm working on adding an HTML-specific accessibility lint rule to biome that enforces meaningful, accessible content in heading elements.

*   The rule must be implemented as a lint rule named 'useHeadingContent' in the 'a11y' category within the biome_html_analyze crate, and must be registered so the spec test infrastructure can discover it.

*   The rule must apply to heading elements h1 through h6 in HTML, Vue, Svelte, and Astro files.

*   In plain HTML files, heading element name matching must be case-insensitive (e.g., H1 and h1 are both treated as heading elements). In Vue, Svelte, and Astro files, only lowercase heading element names (h1–h6) are checked; a heading element whose tag name starts with an uppercase letter is treated as a custom component and ignored.

*   A heading element must produce a diagnostic when it is empty (no children), contains only whitespace text, is self-closing (void-style with no content), or when the heading element itself has the aria-hidden attribute set to 'true'. When aria-hidden is present on the heading element itself, it takes priority over any accessible-name attributes such as aria-label.

*   A heading element must produce a diagnostic when all of its child elements have aria-hidden='true' and there is no other accessible text content.

*   A heading element must NOT produce a diagnostic when it has non-empty, non-whitespace text content; when it carries an aria-label attribute; when it carries an aria-labelledby attribute (HTML); when it carries a title attribute (HTML); when it has nested visible child elements; or when it contains mixed content (some aria-hidden children alongside visible text).

*   In HTML files, a self-closing img child element with a non-empty alt attribute is considered accessible content and must not cause a diagnostic. Img tag name matching for this purpose is case-insensitive in HTML (img, IMG, Img all match).

*   In Vue, Svelte, and Astro files, a child element whose tag name starts with an uppercase letter is treated as a custom component that may render accessible content at runtime, and must not cause a diagnostic — whether it is a paired element or self-closing.

*   When a diagnostic is emitted, the primary message must be exactly: 'Provide screen reader accessible content when using heading elements.' and the note must be exactly: 'All headings on a page should have content that is accessible to screen readers.'


*   Interface details: Type: Rule (Rust lint rule via biome_analyze framework)
Name: UseHeadingContent
Location: crates/biome_html_analyze/src/lint/a11y/use_heading_content.rs
Description: A lint rule that enforces heading elements (h1–h6) have content accessible to screen readers in HTML, Vue, Svelte, and Astro files. Must be declared using the `declare_lint_rule!` macro with `name: "useHeadingContent"`, `language: "html"`, and placed in the `a11y` group. The rule struct must be named `UseHeadingContent`.

Registration requirement: The rule module `use_heading_content` must be declared (i.e., `pub mod use_heading_content;`) in `crates/biome_html_analyze/src/lint/a11y/mod.rs`, and the rule must be registered in the biome_html_analyze rule registry so the spec test infrastructure can discover and execute it.

Diagnostic output (exact strings required by snapshot tests):
- Primary message: "Provide screen reader accessible content when using heading elements."
- Note: "All headings on a page should have content that is accessible to screen readers."
- Rule path shown in diagnostics: `lint/a11y/useHeadingContent`

Spec test directories (must exist and be recognized by the test runner):
- crates/biome_html_analyze/tests/specs/a11y/useHeadingContent/          (HTML tests)
- crates/biome_html_analyze/tests/specs/a11y/useHeadingContent/vue/       (Vue tests)
- crates/biome_html_analyze/tests/specs/a11y/useHeadingContent/svelte/    (Svelte tests)
- crates/biome_html_analyze/tests/specs/a11y/useHeadingContent/astro/     (Astro tests)


**CRITICAL:** Do not modify any files in the `tests/` directory.
The verification system will apply test patches automatically.
Your task is to implement the feature in source files only.
I'll start by exploring the repository structure to understand how HTML lint rules are implemented in biome.

1	//! Shared accessibility helper functions for HTML lint rules.
2	//!
3	//! This module provides reusable utilities for checking accessibility-related
4	//! attributes and element states. All helpers follow a layered architecture:
5	//!
6	//! 1. **Core helpers** (private): Low-level attribute value extraction and checks
7	//! 2. **Element helpers** (public): Higher-level checks on HTML elements
8	//! 3. **Type-specific variants** (public): Optimized versions that avoid cloning
9	
10	use biome_html_syntax::element_ext::AnyHtmlTagElement;
11	use biome_html_syntax::{AnyHtmlElement, HtmlAttribute};
12	
13	// ============================================================================
14	// Core attribute value helpers (private)
15	// ============================================================================
16	
17	/// Checks if an `aria-hidden` attribute has a truthy value.
18	///
19	/// Per ARIA spec, `aria-hidden` accepts only `"true"` or `"false"` as valid values.
20	/// Returns `true` only for non-empty values that are not `"false"` (case-insensitive).
21	/// Missing values, empty strings, and whitespace-only values are considered falsy.
22	///
23	/// Ref: <https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Attributes/aria-hidden>
24	fn is_aria_hidden_value_truthy(attribute: &HtmlAttribute) -> bool {
25	    attribute.value().is_some_and(|value| {
26	        let trimmed = value.trim();
27	        !trimmed.is_empty() && !trimmed.eq_ignore_ascii_case("false")
28	    })
29	}
30	
31	/// Checks if an attribute value equals `"true"` exactly (case-sensitive).
32	fn is_strict_true_value(attribute: &HtmlAttribute) -> bool {
33	    attribute.value().is_some_and(|value| value == "true")
34	}
35	
36	/// Checks if an attribute has a non-empty value after trimming whitespace.
37	///
38	/// Returns `false` for attributes with no value, empty strings, or whitespace-only values.
39	fn has_non_empty_value(attribute: &HtmlAttribute) -> bool {
40	    attribute
41	        .value()
42	        .is_some_and(|value| !value.trim().is_empty())
43	}
44	
45	/// Checks if an attribute value matches the expected string (case-insensitive).
46	///
47	/// Useful for checking HTML attribute values like `type="hidden"` or `role="button"`
48	/// where the comparison should be case-insensitive per HTML spec.
49	pub(crate) fn attribute_value_equals_ignore_case(
50	    attribute: &HtmlAttribute,
51	    expected: &str,
52	) -> bool {
53	    attribute
54	        .value()
55	        .is_some_and(|value| value.eq_ignore_ascii_case(expected))
56	}
57	
58	// ============================================================================
59	// Element-level helpers (public)
60	// ============================================================================
61	
62	/// Returns `true` if the element is hidden from assistive technologies.
63	///
64	/// An element is hidden from screen readers when:
65	/// - It has a truthy `aria-hidden` attribute
66	/// - It is an `<input type="hidden">` element
67	///
68	/// Ref:
69	/// - <https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Attributes/aria-hidden>
70	/// - <https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/input/hidden>
71	/// - <https://github.com/jsx-eslint/eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y/blob/v6.10.0/src/util/isHiddenFromScreenReader.js>
72	pub(crate) fn is_hidden_from_screen_reader(element: &AnyHtmlTagElement) -> bool {
73	    if element
74	        .find_attribute_by_name("aria-hidden")
75	        .is_some_and(|attr| is_aria_hidden_value_truthy(&attr))
76	    {
77	        return true;
78	    }
79	
80	    match element.name_value_token() {
81	        Some(name) if name.text_trimmed() == "input" => element
82	            .find_attribute_by_name("type")
83	            .is_some_and(|attr| attribute_value_equals_ignore_case(&attr, "hidden")),
84	        _ => false,
85	    }
86	}
87	
88	/// Strict check: returns `true` only when `aria-hidden="true"` (case-sensitive).
89	///
90	/// Unlike [`is_aria_hidden_value_truthy`], this only matches the exact string `"true"`.
91	///
92	/// Ref: <https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Attributes/aria-hidden>
93	pub(crate) fn is_aria_hidden_true(element: &AnyHtmlElement) -> bool {
94	    element
95	        .find_attribute_by_name("aria-hidden")
96	        .is_some_and(|attr| is_strict_true_value(&attr))
97	}
98	
99	/// Returns the `aria-hidden` attribute if it has a truthy value.
100	///
101	/// Returns `Some` if present and not `"false"` (case-insensitive), `None` otherwise.
102	/// Useful for code fixes that need to reference the attribute node.
103	///
104	/// Ref: <https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Attributes/aria-hidden>
105	pub(crate) fn get_truthy_aria_hidden_attribute(element: &AnyHtmlElement) -> Option<HtmlAttribute> {
106	    let attribute = element.find_attribute_by_name("aria-hidden")?;
107	    if is_aria_hidden_value_truthy(&attribute) {
108	        Some(attribute)
109	    } else {
110	        None
111	    }
112	}
113	
114	/// Returns `true` if the element has the named attribute with a non-empty value.
115	///
116	/// Whitespace-only values are considered empty.
117	pub(crate) fn has_non_empty_attribute(element: &AnyHtmlElement, name: &str) -> bool {
118	    element

121	}

124	/// `aria-labelledby`, or `title` attributes.
125	pub(crate) fn has_accessible_name(element: &AnyHtmlElement) -> bool {
126	    has_non_empty_attribute(element, "aria-label")

129	}
